subject: math
name: Math
review_note: Draft written for Quark. Grade levels are typical North American placements and vary by curriculum. Needs review by a subject teacher before it is treated as authoritative.

topics.name: Counting and cardinality
learning_goals: Count objects to 20 and beyond, saying one number for each object.
Know that the last number said tells how many are in the set.
key_concepts: Counting on from a known number

misconceptions.description: Counts an object twice or skips one, so the count does not match the set.
misconceptions.example: Counts 7 blocks as '1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8' after touching one block twice.

misconceptions.description: Skips or repeats a number in the counting sequence.

example_problems.prompt: How many stars? (picture of 9 stars)
What number comes after 19?

topics.name: Patterns
learning_goals: Identify, extend and create repeating and growing patterns.
Describe the rule of a pattern in words.

misconceptions.description: Extends a growing pattern as if it repeated.
Misidentifies the core of a repeating pattern.
misconceptions.example: Core of red-red-blue taken as red-blue.

example_problems.prompt: What comes next? 3, 6, 9, 12, __
Extend: circle, square, square, circle, square, square, __

topics.name: Addition and subtraction facts within 20
learning_goals: Add and subtract fluently within 20.
Use strategies such as making ten, doubles and counting on.
key_concepts: Addition and subtraction are inverse operations

misconceptions.description: Recalls an addition or subtraction fact incorrectly.
Believes subtraction can be done in either order.

example_problems.prompt: Sam had 14 stickers and gave away 5. How many are left?

topics.name: Place value to 100
learning_goals: Understand that the digits of a two-digit number stand for tens and ones.
Compare two-digit numbers using place value.

misconceptions.description: Reads the digits without their place value.
Reverses the comparison symbol.

example_problems.prompt: What is the value of the 6 in 64?
Write 3 tens and 8 ones as a number.

topics.name: 2D and 3D shapes
learning_goals: Name and describe common 2D and 3D shapes.
Sort shapes by attributes such as sides, vertices, faces and edges.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a shape stops being a triangle or square when it is rotated.
misconceptions.example: A square turned 45 degrees is called a 'diamond, not a square'.

misconceptions.description: Miscounts the faces or vertices of a solid.

example_problems.prompt: How many sides does a hexagon have?
How many faces does a cube have?

topics.name: Measuring length and telling time
learning_goals: Measure length using standard units and appropriate tools.
Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks.

misconceptions.description: Starts measuring at 1 instead of 0 on the ruler.
misconceptions.example: An object from 1 cm to 6 cm is recorded as 6 cm.

misconceptions.description: Confuses the hour and minute hands.

example_problems.prompt: A pencil starts at 0 cm and ends at 12 cm on a ruler. How long is it?
What time is it when the hour hand is just past 4 and the minute hand points to 6?

topics.name: Pictographs and bar graphs
learning_goals: Collect data and show it in pictographs and bar graphs.
Answer questions by reading and comparing data in a graph.

misconceptions.description: Ignores the key when each picture stands for more than one.
misconceptions.example: Counts 4 pictures as 4 when each picture means 2.

misconceptions.description: Reports a total when asked 'how many more'.
misconceptions.example: Asked how many more chose apples than pears, answers 13 instead of 3.

example_problems.prompt: In a pictograph each icon is 2 votes. Apples has 5 icons. How many votes?

topics.name: Multi-digit addition and subtraction
learning_goals: Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using place value strategies and the standard algorithm.
Estimate to check whether a sum or difference is reasonable.

misconceptions.description: Subtracts the smaller digit from the larger in each column.
Forgets to add the regrouped ten.

topics.name: Place value and rounding of large numbers
learning_goals: Read, write and compare whole numbers to at least one million.
Round whole numbers to a given place.
key_concepts: Each place is ten times the place to its right

misconceptions.description: Rounds by looking at the wrong digit.
misconceptions.example: Rounds 3,462 to the nearest hundred as 3,400 (looked at the ones digit, not the tens).

misconceptions.description: Compares numbers by their first digit regardless of length.

example_problems.prompt: Round 47,385 to the nearest thousand.
Write 300,000 + 5,000 + 20 + 7 in standard form.

topics.name: Multiplication and division facts
learning_goals: Understand multiplication as equal groups and arrays, and division as sharing or grouping.
Know multiplication facts to 10 x 10 and the related division facts.
key_concepts: Division as the inverse of multiplication

misconceptions.description: Recalls a multiplication fact incorrectly.
Treats division as commutative.

example_problems.prompt: 24 pencils are shared equally among 4 students. How many each?

topics.name: Multi-digit multiplication and division
learning_goals: Multiply multi-digit numbers using area models, partial products and the standard algorithm.
Divide with remainders and interpret the remainder in context.

misconceptions.description: Forgets the placeholder zero in the second partial product.
misconceptions.example: 34 x 26: writes 68 instead of 680 for 34 x 20, getting 272.

misconceptions.description: Ignores the context when interpreting a remainder.
misconceptions.example: 45 students, 10 per van: answers 4 vans (remainder 5) instead of 5 vans.

example_problems.prompt: How many boxes of 12 are needed for 100 eggs?

topics.name: Fractions as numbers
learning_goals: Understand a fraction a/b as a parts of size 1/b.
Place fractions on a number line.

misconceptions.description: Counts parts that are not equal in size.
misconceptions.example: Calls one of three unequal pieces 'one third'.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a larger denominator means a larger fraction.

example_problems.prompt: Which is larger, 1/3 or 1/5?
What fraction of a pizza cut into 8 equal slices is 3 slices?

topics.name: Equivalent fractions and comparing fractions
learning_goals: Generate equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same number.
Compare fractions with different denominators.

misconceptions.description: Adds the same number to top and bottom to make an equivalent fraction.
Stops before the fraction is in lowest terms.

example_problems.prompt: Write 3/4 with a denominator of 20.
Simplify 18/24.

topics.name: Adding and subtracting fractions
learning_goals: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers, including unlike denominators.
Solve word problems with fractions.

misconceptions.description: Adds numerators and denominators separately.
Converts the denominator but not the numerator.

topics.name: Multiplying and dividing fractions
learning_goals: Multiply fractions and mixed numbers.
Divide fractions and explain why dividing by a fraction less than 1 gives a larger result.

misconceptions.description: Believes multiplication always makes a number bigger.
misconceptions.example: Says 6 x 1/2 must be more than 6.

misconceptions.description: Flips the wrong fraction when dividing.

topics.name: Decimals and place value
learning_goals: Read, write and compare decimals to thousandths.
Relate decimals to fractions with denominators of 10, 100 and 1000.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a decimal with more digits is larger.
Reads the digits after the point as a whole number.

example_problems.prompt: Which is greater, 0.6 or 0.58?
Write 0.35 as a fraction in lowest terms.

topics.name: Decimal operations
learning_goals: Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals.
Estimate to check the placement of the decimal point.

misconceptions.description: Lines up the last digits instead of the decimal points.
Places the decimal point wrongly in a product.

topics.name: Area and perimeter
learning_goals: Find the perimeter and area of rectangles and composite rectilinear shapes.
Choose the right measure (area or perimeter) for a situation.

misconceptions.description: Finds area when perimeter is asked, or the reverse.
misconceptions.example: A 4 m by 6 m garden needs fencing: answers 24 m.

misconceptions.description: Gives area in linear units or leaves units off.

example_problems.prompt: Find the area and perimeter of a 7 cm by 3 cm rectangle.

topics.name: Line plots and interpreting data
learning_goals: Make line plots and bar graphs with scales.
Solve problems using information in graphs.

misconceptions.description: Reads a bar against the wrong grid line when the scale counts by 2s or 5s.
misconceptions.example: Bar halfway between 10 and 15 read as 11.

misconceptions.description: Gives the category instead of the value.

example_problems.prompt: A bar graph uses a scale of 5. A bar reaches halfway between 20 and 25. What value is it?

topics.name: Angles and angle measurement
learning_goals: Measure and draw angles with a protractor.
Use angle facts: angles on a line, around a point and in a triangle.

misconceptions.description: Reads the wrong scale on the protractor.
misconceptions.example: Measures a 50 degree angle as 130 degrees.

misconceptions.description: Thinks the length of the arms changes the size of the angle.
misconceptions.example: Says the angle with longer arms is bigger.

example_problems.prompt: Two angles of a triangle are 48 and 67 degrees. Find the third.

topics.name: Volume of rectangular prisms
learning_goals: Understand volume as the number of unit cubes that fill a solid.
Use V = l x w x h for rectangular prisms.

misconceptions.description: Adds the dimensions or finds surface area instead of volume.
Uses square units for volume.

example_problems.prompt: Find the volume of a box 5 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm.

topics.name: The coordinate plane
learning_goals: Plot and read points in the coordinate plane, including all four quadrants.
Find horizontal and vertical distances between points.

misconceptions.description: Swaps the x and y coordinates.
Moves the wrong way for a negative coordinate.

example_problems.prompt: What is the distance between (2, -1) and (2, 6)?

topics.name: Order of operations
learning_goals: Evaluate expressions with brackets, exponents, multiplication, division, addition and subtraction.
Insert brackets to make a statement true.
key_concepts: Multiplication and division left to right
Addition and subtraction left to right

misconceptions.description: Works strictly left to right.
Always does multiplication before division (or addition before subtraction).

example_problems.prompt: Evaluate 20 - 3 x (4 + 2).
Evaluate 18 / 3 x 2 + 1.

topics.name: Ratios and unit rates
learning_goals: Use ratio language and tables of equivalent ratios.
Find and compare unit rates.

misconceptions.description: Writes the ratio in the wrong order.
Uses additive instead of multiplicative reasoning.

example_problems.prompt: A car travels 270 km in 3 hours. What is its unit rate?
Which is the better buy: 6 for $4.50 or 10 for $7.20?

topics.name: Percent
learning_goals: Find a percent of a quantity and the whole from a part and a percent.
Solve problems with percent increase, decrease, discounts and tax.

misconceptions.description: Divides by the wrong quantity when finding percent change.
misconceptions.example: Price rises from $40 to $50: says 20% (divided by 50).

misconceptions.description: Thinks successive percent changes add.
misconceptions.example: Up 10% then down 10% returns to the start.

example_problems.prompt: Find 15% of 80.
A $60 jacket is 25% off. What is the sale price?

topics.name: Proportional relationships
learning_goals: Recognise proportional relationships in tables, graphs and equations y = kx.
Solve proportion problems.

misconceptions.description: Calls any straight line proportional, even one not through the origin.
Sets up the proportion with mismatched quantities.
misconceptions.example: 3/5 = x/12 with units flipped on one side

example_problems.prompt: If 4 notebooks cost $10, how much do 10 cost?
y is proportional to x, and y = 21 when x = 3. Find y when x = 8.

topics.name: Integers and signed numbers
learning_goals: Add, subtract, multiply and divide integers.
Use a number line to reason about signed numbers.
key_concepts: Sign rules for multiplication and division

misconceptions.description: Applies a sign rule wrongly.
Applies 'two negatives make a positive' to addition.

topics.name: Algebraic expressions and like terms
learning_goals: Write and evaluate algebraic expressions.
Simplify expressions by collecting like terms and using the distributive property.

misconceptions.description: Combines unlike terms.
Distributes to only the first term in the bracket.

example_problems.prompt: Simplify 4a - 2b + 3a + 5b.
Expand and simplify 2(3x - 1) - (x - 4).

topics.name: Solving one- and two-step equations
learning_goals: Solve one- and two-step linear equations.
Check a solution by substituting it back.

misconceptions.description: Performs an operation on only one side.
Uses the same operation instead of its inverse.

example_problems.prompt: Solve 4x - 7 = 21.
Solve x/5 + 3 = 9.

topics.name: Linear inequalities
learning_goals: Solve linear inequalities and graph the solution on a number line.
Interpret inequality solutions in context.
key_concepts: Reversing the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative

misconceptions.description: Does not reverse the inequality after dividing by a negative.
Uses a closed circle for a strict inequality.
misconceptions.example: x < 4 drawn with a filled dot at 4

example_problems.prompt: Solve 5 - 3x <= 20.

topics.name: Exponent laws and scientific notation
learning_goals: Apply exponent laws for products, quotients, powers, zero and negative exponents.
Write and calculate with numbers in scientific notation.

misconceptions.description: Multiplies exponents when multiplying powers with the same base.
Thinks a negative exponent makes the number negative.

example_problems.prompt: Simplify (3x^2)^3.
Write 0.00045 in scientific notation.

topics.name: Circumference and area of circles
learning_goals: Use C = 2 pi r (or pi d) and A = pi r^2.
Solve problems with circles and parts of circles.

misconceptions.description: Uses the diameter where the radius is needed.
Mixes up the circumference and area formulas.

example_problems.prompt: Find the area of a circle with diameter 12 cm, to one decimal place.

topics.name: Surface area and volume of solids
learning_goals: Find surface area and volume of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres.
Solve optimization-style problems with solids.
key_concepts: Cones and pyramids are one third of the prism

misconceptions.description: Leaves out the 1/3 in cone or pyramid volume.
Uses slant height where perpendicular height is needed.
misconceptions.example: Uses slant 5 instead of height 4 in V = (1/3) pi r^2 h

example_problems.prompt: Find the volume of a cylinder with r = 3 cm and h = 10 cm, in terms of pi.
Find the volume of a sphere with r = 3 cm, in terms of pi.

topics.name: Transformations and congruence
learning_goals: Perform and describe translations, reflections, rotations and dilations.
Use transformations to reason about congruence and similarity.

misconceptions.description: Reflects in the wrong axis.
Rotates in the wrong direction.
misconceptions.example: Rotates 90 degrees clockwise when counter-clockwise was asked.

example_problems.prompt: Reflect (4, -1) in the y-axis.
Dilate (2, 6) by scale factor 1/2 about the origin.

topics.name: Mean, median, mode and range
learning_goals: Calculate and interpret measures of centre and spread.
Choose the most suitable measure for a data set.

misconceptions.description: Finds the median without ordering the data.
Divides by the wrong count when finding the mean.

example_problems.prompt: Find the mean and median of 4, 8, 6, 10, 2.

topics.name: Simple and compound probability
learning_goals: Find theoretical and experimental probabilities.
Use tree diagrams and tables for compound events.

misconceptions.description: Believes past results change independent outcomes (gambler's fallacy).
misconceptions.example: After 4 heads, says tails is more likely.

misconceptions.description: Misses outcomes in the sample space.
misconceptions.example: Two coins: lists HH, HT, TT only.

example_problems.prompt: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability the sum is 7?

topics.name: Linear relations: slope and rate of change
learning_goals: Represent linear relations with tables, graphs and equations.
Interpret slope as a rate of change and the y-intercept as an initial value.

misconceptions.description: Computes slope as run over rise.
Loses a sign when subtracting coordinates.

example_problems.prompt: Find the slope through (-1, 4) and (3, -4).
A taxi charges $3.50 plus $2 per km. Write the relation.

topics.name: Multi-step linear equations
learning_goals: Solve linear equations with variables on both sides, brackets and fractions.
Rearrange formulas for a given variable.

misconceptions.description: Loses a sign when moving a term across the equals sign.
Multiplies only some terms by the common denominator.

example_problems.prompt: Solve 3(x - 2) = 5x + 4.

topics.name: The Pythagorean theorem
learning_goals: Use a^2 + b^2 = c^2 to find a missing side of a right triangle.
Use the converse to test whether a triangle is right-angled.

misconceptions.description: Puts a leg in the hypotenuse position.
misconceptions.example: Legs 5 and 13: 5^2 + 13^2 = c^2 when 13 is the hypotenuse

misconceptions.description: Takes the square root of each term separately.

example_problems.prompt: A right triangle has legs 9 and 12. Find the hypotenuse.
Is a triangle with sides 7, 24, 25 right-angled?

topics.name: Simple and compound interest
learning_goals: Calculate simple interest I = Prt and compound amounts A = P(1 + i)^n.
Compare savings, loans and credit options.

misconceptions.description: Uses the annual rate with monthly periods.
misconceptions.example: Monthly compounding with i = 0.06 and n = 36

misconceptions.description: Uses the percent as a whole number.
misconceptions.example: I = 500 x 4 x 2 instead of 500 x 0.04 x 2

example_problems.prompt: $2,000 is invested at 5% per year compounded annually for 3 years. Find the amount.
Find the simple interest on $800 at 3% per year for 4 years.

topics.name: Scatter plots, correlation and lines of best fit
learning_goals: Make and interpret scatter plots and describe correlation.
Fit a line and use it to make predictions, knowing the limits of extrapolation.

misconceptions.description: Treats correlation as proof of cause.
misconceptions.example: Ice cream sales and drownings rise together, so ice cream causes drowning.

misconceptions.description: Extrapolates far beyond the data.
misconceptions.example: Predicts a 40-year-old's height from children's growth data.

example_problems.prompt: A line of best fit is y = 2.5x + 10. Predict y when x = 8.

topics.name: Equations of lines
learning_goals: Find the equation of a line from a slope and a point, or from two points.
Convert between slope-intercept, point-slope and standard forms; recognise parallel and perpendicular lines.
key_concepts: Parallel slopes are equal; perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals

misconceptions.description: Uses the reciprocal without the sign change for a perpendicular slope.
Drops a sign when solving for b.

example_problems.prompt: Find the equation of the line through (1, 5) and (3, 9).
Find the line perpendicular to y = -1/2 x + 4 through (0, 1).

topics.name: Linear systems
learning_goals: Solve systems of two linear equations by graphing, substitution and elimination.
Interpret the solution, and recognise no-solution and infinite-solution cases.

misconceptions.description: Adds equations when the variable needs subtracting, or multiplies only one side.
misconceptions.example: Eliminating x from 2x + y = 7 and 2x - 3y = -1 by adding.

misconceptions.description: Checks the solution in only one of the original equations.
misconceptions.example: Substitutes (3, 1) into the equation used last and stops.

example_problems.prompt: Solve x + y = 10 and x - y = 4.
Solve 3x + 2y = 16 and x - y = 2.

topics.name: Polynomial operations
learning_goals: Add, subtract and multiply polynomials.
Expand binomial products, including special products.

misconceptions.description: Squares a binomial by squaring each term.
Drops the sign when subtracting a polynomial.

example_problems.prompt: Expand (2x - 3)(x + 4).
Expand (x - 5)^2.

topics.name: Factoring
learning_goals: Factor using a common factor, trinomials, difference of squares and perfect squares.
Check a factorization by expanding.

misconceptions.description: Chooses factors that give the right product but the wrong sum.
Does not factor fully.

example_problems.prompt: Factor x^2 - x - 20.
Factor 6x^2 + 7x - 3.

topics.name: Analytic geometry: distance, midpoint and line segments
learning_goals: Find the length and midpoint of a line segment.
Use them to verify properties of triangles and quadrilaterals and to find equations of medians and bisectors.

misconceptions.description: Mishandles a negative coordinate in the distance formula.
Subtracts coordinates in the midpoint formula.

example_problems.prompt: Find the midpoint and length of the segment from (-2, 1) to (4, 9).

topics.name: Similar triangles
learning_goals: Determine whether triangles are similar and find missing sides.
Solve indirect measurement problems.

misconceptions.description: Matches sides that do not correspond.
misconceptions.example: Pairs the shortest side of one triangle with the longest of the other.

misconceptions.description: Uses differences instead of ratios between similar shapes.

example_problems.prompt: Triangle ABC ~ DEF with AB = 6, DE = 9 and BC = 8. Find EF.

topics.name: Right-triangle trigonometry
learning_goals: Use sine, cosine and tangent to find sides and angles in right triangles.
Solve problems involving angles of elevation and depression.
key_concepts: Opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse depend on the angle

misconceptions.description: Labels opposite and adjacent relative to the wrong angle.
misconceptions.example: Uses tan = 5/12 when the reference angle makes it 12/5.

misconceptions.description: Calculator is in radian mode.

example_problems.prompt: In a right triangle the hypotenuse is 10 and an angle is 30 degrees. Find the side opposite it.
A ladder 6 m long reaches 5 m up a wall. Find the angle with the ground, to the nearest degree.

topics.name: Sine law and cosine law
learning_goals: Use the sine law and cosine law to solve acute (and later obtuse) triangles.
Choose the right law for the information given.
key_concepts: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C

misconceptions.description: Uses the sine law with SAS information.
misconceptions.example: Two sides and the included angle, then a/sin A = ...

misconceptions.description: Subtracts before multiplying in the cosine law.
Misses the second triangle in the ambiguous case.
misconceptions.example: SSA gives only the acute solution.

example_problems.prompt: In triangle ABC, a = 8, b = 11 and C = 60 degrees. Find c, to one decimal place.

topics.name: Quadratic relations and their graphs
learning_goals: Identify key features of a parabola: vertex, axis of symmetry, zeros, direction and optimal value.
Move between standard, factored and vertex forms.

misconceptions.description: Reads the vertex of y = a(x - h)^2 + k with the wrong sign.
Confuses the y-intercept with the vertex.

example_problems.prompt: Find the vertex of y = 2(x - 1)^2 + 5.
Find the zeros of y = (x - 2)(x + 6).

topics.name: Solving quadratic equations
learning_goals: Solve quadratic equations by factoring, the quadratic formula and square roots.
Use the discriminant to find the number of real roots.

misconceptions.description: Takes only the positive square root.
Divides only -b by 2a in the quadratic formula.
Uses the zero product property when the product is not zero.

example_problems.prompt: Solve x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0.
Solve 2x^2 + 3x - 2 = 0.

topics.name: Completing the square and vertex form
learning_goals: Rewrite y = ax^2 + bx + c in vertex form by completing the square.
Use vertex form to find the maximum or minimum value.

misconceptions.description: Adds (b/2)^2 without subtracting it again.
Forgets to multiply the subtracted term by a.

example_problems.prompt: Write y = x^2 + 8x + 3 in vertex form.
Write y = 2x^2 - 12x + 7 in vertex form.

topics.name: Functions, domain and range
learning_goals: Use function notation and decide whether a relation is a function.
State the domain and range, including restricted domains in context.

misconceptions.description: Reads f(x) as f times x.
Ignores values that make the function undefined.
misconceptions.example: Domain of 1/(x - 2) given as all reals

example_problems.prompt: If f(x) = x^2 - 3x, find f(-2).
State the domain of f(x) = sqrt(x - 4).

topics.name: Exponential functions
learning_goals: Graph and interpret exponential growth and decay.
Model situations such as population growth, half-life and compound interest.

misconceptions.description: Treats exponential growth as adding a fixed amount.
Uses the percent instead of the growth factor.

example_problems.prompt: A culture of 500 bacteria doubles every 3 hours. How many after 12 hours?
A car worth $30,000 loses 15% of its value each year. Write its value after t years.

topics.name: Logarithms
learning_goals: Understand the logarithm as the inverse of an exponential function.
Use log laws to solve exponential and logarithmic equations.

misconceptions.description: Splits the log of a sum.
misconceptions.example: log(x + y) = log x + log y

misconceptions.description: Keeps a solution that makes the argument of a log non-positive.

example_problems.prompt: Evaluate log_2 32.
Solve 3^x = 20, to two decimal places.

topics.name: Transformations of functions
learning_goals: Apply translations, stretches, compressions and reflections to parent functions.
Write the equation of a transformed function from its graph.

misconceptions.description: Shifts the wrong way horizontally.
Applies a horizontal shift before factoring out k.

example_problems.prompt: Describe y = -2f(x + 1) - 4 relative to y = f(x).
example_problems.answer: Reflect in the x-axis, vertical stretch by 2, shift left 1 and down 4

topics.name: Polynomial and rational functions
learning_goals: Relate the degree, leading coefficient and factors of a polynomial to its graph.
Find asymptotes and holes of rational functions; solve polynomial and rational inequalities.

misconceptions.description: Treats a removable discontinuity as an asymptote.
misconceptions.example: (x^2 - 4)/(x - 2) has a vertical asymptote at x = 2

misconceptions.description: Misses a sign change interval when solving an inequality.

example_problems.prompt: Find the remainder when x^3 - 2x + 5 is divided by x - 2.
State the vertical and horizontal asymptotes of f(x) = (2x + 1)/(x - 3).

topics.name: Trigonometric functions and identities
learning_goals: Graph sine, cosine and tangent functions and their transformations.
Use radians, the unit circle, and trigonometric identities to solve equations.

misconceptions.description: Finds only one solution of a trig equation in the interval.
misconceptions.example: sin x = 1/2 on [0, 2 pi): x = pi/6 only

misconceptions.description: Computes the period as k instead of 2 pi / k.

example_problems.prompt: Solve 2 cos x = 1 for 0 <= x < 2 pi.
State the period of y = 4 sin(2x).

topics.name: Sequences and series
learning_goals: Find terms and sums of arithmetic and geometric sequences.
Use recursive and explicit formulas.

misconceptions.description: Uses n instead of n - 1 in the general term.
Uses the arithmetic formula for a geometric sequence.

example_problems.prompt: Find the sum of the first 6 terms of 3, 6, 12, ...

topics.name: Counting, permutations and combinations
learning_goals: Use the fundamental counting principle, permutations and combinations.
Calculate probabilities using counting methods.

misconceptions.description: Uses permutations when order does not matter.
Forgets to account for repeated letters.

example_problems.prompt: How many ways can a committee of 4 be chosen from 9 people?
How many arrangements of the letters in BOOK?

topics.name: Probability distributions and the normal distribution
learning_goals: Work with discrete distributions, expected value and the binomial distribution.
Use z-scores and the normal distribution to find probabilities.

misconceptions.description: Divides by the variance instead of the standard deviation.
Gives P(Z < z) when P(Z > z) was asked.

example_problems.prompt: Scores are normal with mean 70 and sd 8. What is the z-score of 86?
A fair coin is tossed 4 times. Find P(exactly 2 heads).

topics.name: Sampling, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests
learning_goals: Describe sampling methods and bias.
Construct and interpret confidence intervals and carry out a significance test.

misconceptions.description: States the conclusion without referring to the p-value or context.
Reads a 95% confidence interval as a 95% chance the parameter is in this interval.
misconceptions.example: 'There is a 95% probability the true mean is between 4.1 and 5.3.'

example_problems.prompt: A sample of 100 has mean 52 and the population sd is 10. Find the 95% confidence interval for the mean (z* = 1.96).

topics.name: Vectors
learning_goals: Represent vectors geometrically and algebraically and add, subtract and scale them.
Use the dot product (and cross product, where taught) to find angles and projections.

misconceptions.description: Adds magnitudes of non-parallel vectors.
Loses a sign in a component.

example_problems.prompt: Find the magnitude of (6, -8).

topics.name: Limits and continuity
learning_goals: Evaluate limits numerically, graphically and algebraically.
Decide where a function is continuous.

misconceptions.description: Thinks 0/0 means the limit does not exist.
Ignores that left and right limits differ.
misconceptions.example: Gives one value for a jump discontinuity

example_problems.prompt: Evaluate lim (x^2 - 9)/(x - 3) as x -> 3.

topics.name: Derivatives and differentiation rules
learning_goals: Understand the derivative as an instantaneous rate of change and slope of the tangent.
Differentiate using the power, product, quotient and chain rules.

misconceptions.description: Forgets the inner derivative in the chain rule.
Differentiates a product as the product of derivatives.

example_problems.prompt: Differentiate f(x) = 4x^3 - 5x + 2.
Differentiate y = (2x + 1)^5.

topics.name: Applications of derivatives
learning_goals: Use derivatives to find maxima, minima and points of inflection and to sketch curves.
Solve optimization and related-rates problems.

misconceptions.description: Does not check endpoints in a closed-interval optimization.
misconceptions.example: Reports a local max as the absolute max

misconceptions.description: Finds the critical value but does not answer the question asked.
misconceptions.example: Finds x = 5 but never states the maximum area

example_problems.prompt: Find the maximum area of a rectangle with perimeter 40 m.

topics.name: Integrals and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
learning_goals: Find antiderivatives and evaluate definite integrals.
Interpret a definite integral as accumulated change or signed area.

misconceptions.description: Leaves out the constant of integration.
Subtracts in the wrong order when evaluating.
misconceptions.example: F(a) - F(b) instead of F(b) - F(a)

example_problems.prompt: Evaluate the integral of 3x^2 from 0 to 2.
Find the integral of (4x - 1) dx.
